run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T08:55:56Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on frontend-proxy is backed by a real error burst: frontend-proxy ingress error spans rose from 0–1.3 per 2 minutes to 64–184 per 2 minutes between 08:56 and 09:06 (evidence a178b2d5-2a1c-4e8e-af2d-eed7152b2fa3-t1:a2ccd50e-840c-4b89-a666-c83e6d43f867). The error spans trace one path only: frontend API routes /api/cart and /api/checkout and their gRPC calls to cart and checkout (evidence 3517681e-8162-439e-b3fd-240ddf298f2d-t1:4d37067e-3f84-44c8-9c92-313868b0cd55). Cart's own container logs show the failing operation: repeated "Wasn't able to connect to redis" from 08:56:15 onward against VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 (evidence 52c403f8-4c57-4eaa-b44f-b8e4dae0bf88-t3:eb181195-70d1-45dc-87c9-f649f2608f85, eff9d04b-06c7-4c17-9907-4dfbe483d120-t0:97142fd7-c6ca-4850-bdb9-b082c8df121c). The dependency, valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr, also stopped answering the otel-collector's Redis receiver on a different node at the same minute: redis_cpu_time_seconds_total{state="user"} froze at 2.6249 from 08:54:30 and redis_memory_used_bytes froze at 1,710,360 from 08:55:00, while the same collector kept exporting rising spanmetrics (evidence 5040e4f3-a030-4996-888d-107c4ab59786-t0:73108998-5566-4c15-aafb-2c2aa7df1f7d, 998889a1-68cb-4b14-91d1-e4cca28db635-t1:58edd023-1adb-446f-90c5-5ebdb8cb8ca8, 125923ef-19cf-4ba6-b134-a9cb898d1734-t0:e41ccc0d-42e0-4929-81c0-0fb70e83b5a9). The pod stayed Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and no OOMKill, its cgroup never approached its 10Mi memory limit and was only mildly CPU-throttled, so why Redis stopped serving is not established: it remains a hypothesis that a pod-level network fault or an internal stall at valkey-cart blocked clients, with cart's CPU throttling (45m limit, 0.83–0.90 of CFS periods) an alternative explanation for the client-side connect failures. Telemetry stops advancing at ~09:05:30, so recovery is not observable.

claims.text: The alerting signal is a real burst: frontend-proxy ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans were 0–1.33 per 2 minutes between 08:47 and 08:55, then 64 at 08:56:00, 140 at 08:57:00 and a peak of 184 at 09:03:00, back to 0 at 09:06:00.

Over the 07:55:56–09:11:59 window frontend-proxy recorded 961.3 error-status ingress spans (extrapolated increase) against 16,215.8 UNSET ingress spans; ingress was its only error-bearing operation and 'router frontend egress' had 0 error spans.

Error spans in the window are confined to the cart call chain: frontend GET /api/cart 31.5, POST /api/cart 46.3, POST /api/checkout 7.1, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 46.3, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 31.5, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 7.1; cart POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 45.2 and POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 38.8; checkout oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 6.75 and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 6.75.

Cart's container logs repeat "Wasn't able to connect to redis" and "Error status code '{StatusCode}' with detail '{Detail}' raised." from 08:56:15 onward, each typically seconds after a GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync call; the last readable matching line is 09:02:32.
Cart is configured with VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 and runs on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae; the valkey-cart pod (IP 100.96.2.228) runs on the same node.
valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, state.running.startedAt 08:22:53 and an empty lastState; its Deployment template declares no liveness or readiness probes.
The valkey-cart Service (clusterIP 100.68.233.28, port 6379) has a ready endpoint 100.96.2.228:6379 targeting valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr.
Container resource limits are cart cpu 45m / memory 165Mi and valkey-cart cpu 10m / memory 10Mi (requests cart 15m/55Mi, valkey-cart 2m/4Mi).

valkey-cart's cgroup stayed well inside those limits during the window: memory working set 3.48–4.20 MB, max usage 5.05–5.69 MB, memory failcnt 0, CPU ~0.002–0.003 cores, and only 1.1–6.2% of CFS periods throttled.

The otel-collector's Redis receiver targets valkey-cart:6379 with a 10s collection interval, and its exported valkey counters stopped advancing at the same minute cart failed: redis_cpu_time_seconds_total{state="user"} rose to 2.6249 at 08:54:30 and then stayed exactly 2.6249 through 09:03:30, while redis_memory_used_bytes flattened at 1,710,360 from 08:55:00 and redis_memory_peak_bytes at 1,726,344 from 08:56:00.

The collector itself continued working while the Redis series were frozen: its container memory working set was ~223–232 MB of a 300Mi limit and its spanmetrics counters kept increasing to 22,390 (frontend-proxy ingress UNSET) at 09:05:00 before going flat.

The cart container's own CPU throttling rose sharply during the incident: throttled CFS period ratio went from ~0.17–0.24 before 08:56 to 0.44 at 08:56:56, 0.74 at 08:58:56 and 0.83–0.90 through 09:06:56, with cart usage rising from ~0.010 to ~0.026 cores against its 45m limit.

The old pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s on node i-00702f4ac4662cf00 (a different node from cart and valkey) recorded 75 Killing events and 30 Warning FailedKillPod events reporting KillContainer/KillPodSandbox DeadlineExceeded, the last at 08:58:46; it no longer exists and the cart Endpoints list only cart-755465879b-t9mf7.

No pod in otel-demo restarted or was recreated during the window (all 21 pods Running, restart counts 0); the only pod created cluster-wide between 08:40 and 09:11:59 is clickhouse-unified-recorder-kqdh5 in data-recorders at 09:01:53.

The failing dependency is valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr: two independent clients on different nodes, cart on i-0146cb0d0caf26bae and the otel-collector on i-0a709b85c49d987be, lost the valkey-cart:6379 endpoint within the same minute around 08:55 while the pod stayed Running with no restart, and cart's resulting 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' failures propagate to frontend /api/cart errors and the frontend-proxy ingress error spans.

The fault originates at the valkey-cart Redis instance: something stopped it answering clients at ~08:55 (a pod-level network fault that blackholed port 6379, or an internal stall of the valkey process). Cart's quickly repeated connect failures and the frozen Redis counters seen from another node both fit this; the specific mechanism is not visible in the available telemetry.

Cart's own 45m CPU limit and the observed 0.83–0.90 CFS throttling could have starved the .NET Redis client so that its connect attempts exceeded their timeout, making the cart Deployment's CPU limit a cart-side cause; this does not explain why valkey stopped advancing its own counters for the collector on another node.

valkey-cart's 10Mi memory limit is close to the 9,744,384-byte RSS that valkey itself reported (redis_memory_rss_bytes), so memory pressure on the valkey process is a candidate trigger; cAdvisor's own working-set reading of 3.5–4.2 MB, zero memory failcnt and no OOM/restart do not support it.

The flagd fault-injection flag 'cartFailure' (description 'Fail cart service') is a candidate because it declares a cart failure; however the flagd-config ConfigMap currently sets cartFailure to defaultVariant off, its value during the window could not be read, and the failure cart logged is a Redis connectivity failure rather than a flag-driven cart error.
valkey-cart did not restart or get OOM-killed: restartCount 0, empty lastState, container running continuously since 08:22:53.
Resource exhaustion of valkey-cart is not supported: max cgroup memory usage 5.69 MB against the 10Mi limit, memory failcnt 0 throughout, and CPU throttling never above ~6.2% of periods.

A node-wide or cluster-wide failure is not supported: error spans exist only for cart, checkout, frontend and frontend-proxy cart-dependent operations, while product-catalog, recommendation, currency, payment, shipping and email recorded no error spans beyond 2–3 background flagd EventStream errors over 76 minutes, and CPU throttling at 09:02 was 0.83 only for cart versus 0.095 for product-catalog, 0.093 for frontend and 0.013 for payment.

The FailedKillPod/Killing events on cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s are not the cause of this error burst: that pod ran on node i-00702f4ac4662cf00 (different from cart and valkey on i-0146cb0d0caf26bae), it is no longer in the cart Endpoints, and its kill attempts were already running at the start of the event window (08:38:44), about 17 minutes before cart's first Redis error at 08:56:15.

A rollout or restart of cart or valkey-cart is not the cause: no otel-demo pod was recreated during the window, cart and valkey-cart restart counts are 0, and the only pod created cluster-wide between 08:40 and 09:11:59 is clickhouse-unified-recorder-kqdh5 in data-recorders.

Retrieve valkey-cart's container logs (currently empty via the log API) and the kubelet/containerd logs of node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae for 08:55–09:06, and inspect CNI flow logs (Cilium/Hubble) for drops between 100.96.2.233 (cart) or the collector and 100.96.2.228:6379, to determine whether the Redis endpoint was network-blackholed or the process stalled.

Add a readiness probe to the valkey-cart Deployment (currently none) so a non-responsive Redis instance is visible on the pod, and review the unusually small cart cpu 45m and valkey-cart cpu 10m / memory 10Mi limits; raising the cart CPU limit would also test the throttling hypothesis.

gaps: valkey-cart's application logs could not be read (fetch_pod_logs returned 0 lines for the container), so the reason the Redis endpoint stopped answering is unknown.

The query for NetworkPolicies in otel-demo returned nothing (status no_data), so whether a policy change blocked cart or the collector from reaching valkey-cart on port 6379 could not be verified either way.
The RequestErrorRate alerting rule was not returned by list_prometheus_rules (no alerting rules came back), so the exact expression and threshold behind the 1.0888 reading are unknown.

Jaeger retained traces only from about 09:03:21 onward (frontend-proxy spans start at 09:03:21 and cart searches for 08:56–09:07 returned nothing), so error detail fields for the failure window are unavailable.

kube-state-metrics series are absent from this Prometheus (queries for kube_* metric names and for kube_deployment_status_replicas_available returned nothing), so pod/deployment state history during the window cannot be verified from metrics.

Span and Redis metric series stop advancing at about 09:05:30 and 09:03:30 respectively, so whether and when cart and valkey-cart recovered is not observable; the apparent end of the error burst coincides with telemetry stopping.
The change_history integration is not available and no change/chaos history is exposed, so whether a fault injection or configuration change targeted valkey-cart at 08:55 cannot be verified.
Redis credentials in the otel-collector configuration are redacted, so an authentication-related Redis failure cannot be excluded.
No events exist for the valkey-cart pod in the window and events expire, so any kubelet or runtime event affecting it may be missing.
next_steps: Read valkey-cart container logs and node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae kubelet/containerd logs for 08:55–09:06 to establish why Redis stopped answering.
Check CNI flow telemetry (Cilium/Hubble) for packet drops to and from valkey-cart pod IP 100.96.2.228 port 6379 during 08:55–09:06.
List NetworkPolicies in otel-demo with a tool that returns them, to confirm whether policy changes affected the cart-to-valkey-cart path.
Confirm from change/chaos history whether a network or resource fault was applied to valkey-cart or cart at 08:55.

Reproduce under current limits: probe valkey-cart with redis-cli PING/INFO while cart is under load to separate a network blackhole from a process stall, and evaluate the effect of the 10m CPU / 10Mi memory valkey limits and the 45m cart CPU limit.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.

content.value:
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:
    - default: otel-demo
      name: namespace
exporters:
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: http://clickhouse-clickhouse.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local:8123
    logs_table_name: otel_demo_logs
    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    endpoint: http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090
    tls:
      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - nginx
      - otlp
      - postgresql
      - redis
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - pull:
          exporter:
            prometheus:
              host: 0.0.0.0
              port: 8888
